# {{delivery}} lane brief

**Epic: {{headline}}. These are the lane rules.**

<!-- Generated by `run_delivery.py lead-brief` from {{config}}, the delivery file and the run-delivery templates. Edit those, not this file. -->

The mechanical steps are `run-delivery` commands: `{{flow}} <command>`, run from your own checkout. Use them. Don't
assemble briefs, round files or records by hand, and don't edit what they write.

## Plan

- The approved plan is `{{plan}}`. Read your story in the tracker ({{tracker}}), then its section in the plan and
  the plan's decisions. The decisions are binding: raise a disagreement with the lead; don't redesign.
- The first approved stories become references. Once the lead names one, follow its shape.

## Repository

- Read the repository's root instruction file first. Its rules apply.
- Each story gets its own checkout from the delivery base. From the main checkout:
  `git fetch {{remote}} && git worktree add --no-track -b {{branch}} {{lane_checkout}} {{base_ref}}`, then run the
  repository's prepare step there. Use exactly that path: the lead reads your gate and in-app evidence from it.
  Never edit the lead's checkout or another lane's.
- Never merge or rebase `{{base_ref}}` into your branch once it exists. A new head means another gate run, review
  round and PR review. You don't need the base: `{{flow}}` reads the delivery's plan, brief and settings from
  `{{base_ref}}` itself, so the lead's changes reach you without a merge, and the merge queue syncs your branch with
  the base when it merges. If the queue reports a real conflict, the lead returns the story to you, and only then do
  you merge the base.
- Branch: `{{branch}}`. Commit subjects start with the story key.
- Never touch: {{never_touch}}. Change only the files your lane owns (below, and `lanes.<lane>.owns` in
  the delivery file). The lead refuses a hand-off that changes anything else.
- Long commands (gates, builds, in-app checks) can take minutes: run them in the background or with a long timeout,
  never under a short tool timeout.

## The focused lane profile

1. Write the story's scenarios first (test-first or characterization-first, as the plan says). Every test must assert
   something.
2. Commit, then run the gates: `{{flow}} gate <key>`. It runs, in order:
{{gates}}
   and records the result against your HEAD. The hand-off needs a passing run at the head you hand off.
3. Run the story's in-app checks, if the repository declares them (see In-app checks).
4. Review (see Review) until every lens approves, within {{bound}} rounds. At the bound, stop and report the blocker
   to the lead.
5. Compounding: note anything reusable for the lead in the PR body or the hand-off's `--findings`.
6. Push your own branch and open its draft PR into `{{base_branch}}`: `{{flow}} push <key>`, then
   `{{flow}} open-pr <key> --title "<key>: <summary>" --body-file <file>` (Summary, Why, Validation; the tracker link
   is added if missing). Both refuse what the authority below doesn't grant.

   **Authority.** {{authority}}
{{pr_review}}7. Hand off (see Hand-off).

The review must see the final code, and the gates and in-app checks must have run on it. If anything changes after a
round, run another round; re-run the gates at the new head, and the in-app checks if shipped files changed.
{{in_app}}
## Review

Lenses {{lenses}}, through `obtain-review`/`review-work`, realized by host convention as reviewers the lane starts and
resumes. `run-delivery` does the mechanical part.

1. Before round 1, fill in "Evidence so far" in `{{work}}/review/<key>/context.md`. `review-prepare` seeds it
   from the plan the first time it runs and refuses until you replace the TODO line. Update it before each later round.
2. `{{flow}} review-prepare <key> --round <n>` makes one private, prepared checkout per lens at your HEAD and one filled
   round brief per lens. Commit first: it refuses uncommitted or untracked files.
3. Round 1: start one reviewer per lens in parallel with the prompts it prints, and keep track of each. Later rounds:
   resume the same reviewers with the new prompts. Save each final JSON message, exactly as returned, to the result path it
   printed. Never write or edit a result yourself. A prepared round can't be prepared again: reduce it. If you must
   discard it (the candidate was wrong, say), `--restart` does, and the lead has to accept every restart.
4. `{{flow}} review-reduce <key> --round <n>` checks each result against its brief, assembles the round file, checks it
   with the release's own validator, journals the round, removes the lens checkouts, and prints the verdict, the open
   and deferred findings, and the tracker post. A result that doesn't match its brief is kept as an attempt and the
   round refused: re-run only that lens with the same brief; the other results stand. Attempts are recorded.
5. Fix the blocking findings, commit, and go to step 2 with the next round. At the bound without alignment the round
   is `blocked`: stop and tell the lead (a grace round, `--grace`, needs the lead's say-so).
6. If you ever lose your review folder (a recreated checkout, say), tell the lead: the lead-side log still has your
   earlier preparations, and the lead decides on them at acceptance.

Triage: blocking (P0/P1) findings are always fixed in the lane. Lenses file P2/P3 as deferred, with what the follow-up
must say: fix the cheap ones in the lane anyway, and pass the expensive ones to the lead with `--findings`. A finding
first raised in a later round, against code an earlier round approved, is judged on scope before it blocks.

## Hand-off

`{{flow}} handoff <key> --pr <PR link> [--findings "<expensive non-blocking findings>"] [--blocked <name>=<reason> ...]`

Every `--blocked` item, and every restarted review round, is the lead's decision: the lead accepts each one by
name, or sends the story back. It refuses unless the checkout is clean (untracked files included), your branch on `{{remote}}` is at HEAD, the PR is
open from your branch into `{{base_branch}}`, the last round has every lens approving exactly that head, the gates
passed at it, and the in-app evidence is complete and current. Then it captures the review rounds, hands off to the
record, and prints the hand-off message and the tracker post. Send the lead that message, word for word. Don't merge
or release. The lead verifies the claims and accepts; the merge queue merges after syncing your branch with the base.

## Tracker updates

Post on your own story with your tracker tools: at start, at each decision you make (what and why), at each review
round (`review-reduce` prints the text), at each finding you pass to the lead, and at hand-off (`handoff` prints the
text). One attempt each, never a gate.

{{transitions}}

## Focus

Say what you're doing as it changes, with the installed release's state tool:
`python3 -B .agent-skills/current/skills/orchestrate-work/scripts/delivery_state.py --dir {{state}} focus --lane <lane> --text "<what you are doing>" [--state working|reviewing|blocked] [--waiting-on <who>]`.
`review-prepare` sets `reviewing` for you.

## Questions

Escalate only to the lead, never to the user: one short question, then stop. The lead answers, or takes it to the user.
